news.title: SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters
news.summary_raw:
AI agents often fail because their instructions, or skills, are manually modified with no guarantee of improvement. Learn how SkillOpt turns skill editing into a training process, making agent behavior more reliable without changing model weights.
The post SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has developed SkillOpt, a technique that turns skill editing into a training process for AI agents. This makes agent behavior more reliable without modifying model weights.
news.enterprise_use: Watch for potential integration of SkillOpt in future Microsoft 365 or Azure releases, enabling AI agents with trainable parameters to improve behavior without manual modification. This could enhance Microsoft's bot services and improve agent reliability. Missing out on this technology means potential reliance on outdated or manually modified AI agents.

news.title: Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity
news.summary_raw:
AI agents can't remember past conversations. They must constantly reload or retrieve context, which grows less efficient as tasks get longer and more complex. Memora solves this with a scalable memory system separating what’s stored from how it's retrieved.
The post Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research's Memora is a new memory representation system designed to improve the efficiency of AI agents. Memora decouples storage from retrieval, making it easier for agents to access and recall context in long and complex tasks.
news.enterprise_use: Note your interest in Microsoft Research's advancements in AI memory representation, as this technology could lead to future innovations in SSO and authentication workflows, potentially improving security and usability.
